about: Globe pins for jihe-yuanben. lat/lon are copied from BRIEF.md section 1, 'Coordinates for the globe build' (decimal degrees, north and east positive). caption is the on-screen coordinate string the brief's script uses (two decimals). dates quote the post (BRIEF.md section 2) unless 'source' names another part of the brief. name_zh labels are standard place names added for typesetting; BRIEF.md does not give them, so check them before the film states them.

dates.text: Around 1590, in Shaozhou, he worked through Book I with the scholar Qu Rukui. That manuscript is lost.

places.name: Beijing
places.site: Jesuit residence near Xuanwumen (site of the later South Cathedral)
places.caption: 39.90° N, 116.37° E · Beijing · 1606

dates.text: Every afternoon from the autumn of 1606, Xu went to Ricci's residence near Xuanwumen.
The six books were printed in Beijing in 1607.
In 1611 Xu revised the text with the Jesuits Sabatino de Ursis and Diego de Pantoja, working from Ricci's annotated copy.
dates.source: post (the post does not say where the revision was made)

places.notes: The site is confirmed; the 1606 building footprint is not (BRIEF.md). Pin the site, not a building.
